item.title: Applied Digital names Brookwood, Alabama as Delta Forge 2 site for 210 MW leased AI campus
item.description: On 24 September 2026 Applied Digital confirmed that Delta Forge 2 — previously disclosed only as a 'new southern state' campus in its 8 June 2026 IR lease release — will be built in Brookwood, Tuscaloosa County, Alabama (~1.26 million sq ft on about 160 acres of a nearly 1,300-acre site). The campus carries the existing 210 MW critical-IT 15-year take-or-pay lease with an unnamed U.S. investment-grade hyperscaler (~$5.2B base-term contracted revenue per the June IR). Combined company-plus-tenant investment is stated above $3.2 billion (TCEDA/TCIDA fact sheet ~$3.2865B). The Tuscaloosa County Economic Development Authority unanimously approved an incentive package of roughly $314.5 million in tax abatements plus $270 million in community-benefit payments over 20 years. Construction is scheduled to begin about 1 October 2026 with completion targeted by end-2028; tenant identity and final County Commission / Brookwood City Council incentive votes remain open. Country conversion: USA Alabama geography unlock plus local incentive package for a named 210 MW AI Factory campus that had no public state/site before 24 Sep. [Signal 84, Corroborated, via WBRC / ABC 33/40 / Tuscaloosa Thread (quoting Applied Digital + TCEDA); lease MW from Applied Digital IR 8 Jun 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: BDx breaks ground on 640 MW CGK4 AI campus in West Java with 845 MVA PLN power
item.description: On 22 September 2026 BDx Data Centers announced groundbreaking on AI Campus 2 (CGK4) in Jatiluhur, West Java, Indonesia: a planned 640 MW AI data-center campus backed by 845 MVA of grid capacity from PLN (part of BDx's stated 1.2 GVA+ secured Indonesia AI-campus power position). Construction has begun on Building 1 of six planned buildings; Building 1 is designed for 120 MW IT capacity in phases, with the first contracted phase expected to enter service in early 2027, using direct-to-chip liquid cooling rated up to 500 kW per rack. West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi and Purwakarta Regent Saepul Bahri Binzein attended. Country conversion: Indonesia adds a named, power-backed AI campus groundbreak with a near-term first-building service window — no named hyperscaler tenant disclosed in the company release. [Signal 90, Confirmed, via BDx Data Centers via PR Newswire] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: New Era (NUAI) TCDC PowerCo signs 20-year 200–207 MW PPA with Vistra/Luminant for Odessa Phase 1
item.description: On 18 September 2026 (8-K filed 21 Sep) TCDC PowerCo LLC, a New Era Energy & Digital subsidiary, entered a Power Purchase Agreement with Luminant ET Services (Vistra affiliate) for a minimum 200 MW and up to 207 MW of energy for Phase 1 of the Texas Critical Data Center near Odessa. Supply is primarily from Vistra's adjacent 1,180 MW Odessa gas plant (or other sources/ERCOT). Initial term 20 years from first Delivery Date; press says contracted power expected available Q3 2027. Credit support: $116M letter of credit within 15 business days of PPA date plus additional security not to exceed $82.8M by Delivery Date (~$198.8M ceiling). Concurrent DFA grants Vistra ROFR on future onsite generation and 5% non-voting Project Company equity once power flows. Campus: 493-acre Permian site with pathway cited to ~1.4 GW; construction permits claimed in Ex.99.1; no named tenant in the September announcement. Country conversion: Permian Phase 1 power is now under a filed 20-year PPA with posted security schedule — Energy/Build for USA, still pre-tenant and pre-delivery. [Signal 91, Confirmed, via New Era Energy & Digital Form 8-K (filed 21 Sep 2026; event 18 Sep) + Ex.99.1] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Kodiak Gas Services contracts 76 MW behind-the-meter baseload to West Texas data center (6-year)
item.description: On 21 September 2026 Kodiak Gas Services (NYSE: KGS) announced a six-year agreement to provide 76 MW of behind-the-meter baseload power capacity, including balance of plant, to a West Texas data center. Deployment: ~40 reciprocating natural-gas generation units beginning Q4 2026 and scaling into Q1 2027, with revenue recognition expected to start Q1 2027. Counterparty described only as a data-center operator contracted with an investment-grade-rated hyperscaler, with a GPU designer as guarantor of the data-center lease — names not disclosed. Kodiak calls this its second long-term primary-power data-center contract; about half of its current power portfolio is now under long-term power contracts. Country conversion: 76 MW BTM gas generation contracted for a hyperscaler-backed West Texas campus with a near-term deploy window — Energy/Build for USA without a named tenant or campus MW beyond the power block. [Signal 86, Confirmed, via Kodiak Gas Services IR press release (21 Sep 2026)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Abbott directs TCEQ to halt all Texas data-center permits pending ERCOT/TWDB audits
item.description: On 21 September 2026 Governor Greg Abbott directed Texas Commission on Environmental Quality Executive Director Kelly Keel to pause issuance of all permits related to data-center projects until ERCOT completes its Large Load review (with TWDB water-use work in parallel). The letter states no other state agency should move forward with data-center regulatory approvals until PUC/ERCOT/TWDB audit information is acquired, and requires TCEQ to update the Governor's office on compliance by Monday 19 October 2026. Country conversion: Texas extends the August interconnect freeze into statewide environmental permitting, widening the stall on AI campus build timelines beyond ERCOT queue gating alone. [Signal 93, Confirmed, via Office of the Governor of Texas (letter PDF)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Fluidstack says construction begun on $4B / up to 1.5 GW Cameron County first phase
item.description: On 21 September 2026 Fluidstack published that it has begun construction on the $4 billion first phase of an AI data-center campus in Cameron County, Texas, planned to support up to 1.5 GW of capacity, with more than 2,500 expected construction jobs. Cameron County earlier (10 Sep) issued a worksite permit for site preparation near Valley International Airport; the county notice says future permits are still required before building construction. Fluidstack says it requested no local tax abatement, will pay for energy/infrastructure/water, and will participate in PUCT/ERCOT audits under Abbott directives. Country conversion: a named Texas AI campus moves from permit talk into company-stated construction start on a multi-GW phase, still under the broader Abbott/TCEQ permitting freeze and county building-permit gates. [Signal 84, Corroborated, via Fluidstack company post (+ Cameron County worksite permit)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: PUCT adopts 16 TAC §25.194 large-load interconnection rule ($50k/MW security; ≥75 MW)
item.description: On 18 September 2026 the Public Utility Commission of Texas filed Order Adopting new 16 TAC §25.194 (Interchange Project 58481 item 218), implementing PURA §37.0561 / SB 6 Large Load Interconnection Standards for ERCOT. Before inclusion in an ERCOT interconnection study, a large-load customer must execute an intermediate agreement, disclose, and post financial security of $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand; a Standard Large Load Interconnection Agreement (SLLIA), further security, and CIAC follow after study. The rule covers customers at or above the 75 MW large-load threshold. Same-day item 219 is the Texas Register Acknowledgement of Receipt (TRD 202604027) for the 10/02/2026 issue; Interchange describes effectiveness as of 10.08.2026. Country conversion: Texas’s permanent ≥75 MW interconnect rule is now stamped — Batch Zero and subsequent large-load queues run under a live security and disclosure regime rather than staff draft. [Signal 92, Confirmed, via PUCT Interchange 58481 item 218 Order Adopting; item 219 Texas Register ack] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: PUCT files written Order on Howard–Solstice 765 kV (59336) — Route 4 mod 1 CCN
item.description: On 18 September 2026 PUCT OPDM filed the written Order in Docket 59336 (Interchange item 2741), amending AEP Texas CCN 30028 and CPS Energy CCN 30031 to build and operate the Howard-to-Solstice ~370-mile 765 kV single-circuit line along Route 4 mod 1 (not SOAH’s recommended Route 4). The Order cites lower estimated cost/length vs Route 4, ~60.3 miles (16.53%) paralleling existing ROW, and an estimated line cost of $2.15 billion for Route 4 mod 1; authority runs seven years unless energized sooner. This stamps the 11 Sep open-meeting approval that prior Wire tracked as pending written order. Country conversion: Permian Basin Reliability Plan southern import path moves from press-confirmed vote to operable CCN order. [Signal 90, Confirmed, via PUCT Interchange 59336 item 2741 Order (filed 18 Sep 2026)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: CleanSpark prices $2.276B 7.875% senior notes (upsized) to finish Meta-anchored Sandersville AI campus
item.description: On 18 September 2026 CleanSpark filed an 8-K with Exhibit 99.1 stating subsidiary CSDC Finance I, LLC priced a $2.276 billion offering of 7.875% senior secured notes due 2031 at 98.500% of principal (upsized from the 17 Sep proposed $2.227B). Expected close 25 September 2026 subject to customary conditions. Net proceeds fund remaining Sandersville data-center build-out, reimburse prior equity contributions, and fund debt-service reserves; CSRE Properties Sandersville guarantees; CleanSpark provides a completion guarantee. Follows the 17 Sep disclosure naming Meta subsidiary Anviran as tenant on the 175 MW Georgia lease. Country conversion: construction finance for a named Meta AI campus moves from proposed offering to priced notes — Capital/Build for Georgia CNW Realized still conditional on close. [Signal 88, Confirmed, via CleanSpark Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (filed 18 Sep 2026)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: RWE signs 433 MW West Texas VPPA with Oracle for AI data-center power
item.description: On 17 September 2026 RWE Americas announced a virtual power purchase agreement with Oracle for 433 MW from existing Panther Creek I, II and III wind farms in Sterling, Howard and Glasscock counties (West Texas). RWE says the VPPA is part of Oracle’s broader Texas power portfolio totaling more than 1.7 GW supporting the ERCOT grid for Oracle data-center operations. Country conversion: a named hyperscaler locks another hundreds-of-MW renewable hedge onto Texas generation that already exists — firming Oracle’s Texas AI load path without waiting on new interconnect alone. [Signal 88, Confirmed, via RWE Americas press release] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: CleanSpark names Meta (Anviran) as 175 MW Sandersville AI tenant; proposes $2.227B notes
item.description: On 17 September 2026 CleanSpark disclosed in investor materials accompanying an SEC filing that Anviran LLC — tenant on its 175 MW Sandersville, Georgia campus under a previously announced 20-year triple-net lease (~$6.6B expected revenue over the initial term) — is a wholly owned Meta Platforms subsidiary, with Meta guaranteeing rent and opex. item.title: Anthropic signs first Australia lease at Zerra Western Downs (path to 2.16 GW peak)
item.description: On 16 September 2026, Queensland Premier David Crisafulli announced in Parliament that Anthropic signed its first Australian data-centre lease as anchor tenant at Singapore developer Zerra DC’s proposed Western Downs Digital Park near Dalby (~250 km from Brisbane). Planning docs put IT capacity at ~1.44 GW across four halls and peak grid draw about 2.16 GW at full build; Reuters (sources) and ABC report first use targeted 2027 for inference (not training), closed-loop/air-cooled design, and FIRB + Western Downs Regional Council approvals still outstanding. Anthropic and Zerra declined comment to Reuters. Country conversion: Australia gets a named frontier-lab lease on a GW-class campus — still FIRB/council/power gated, not energization. [Signal 84, Reuters Sydney 16 Sep (anonymous sources; Anthropic/Zerra no comment). Premier Crisafulli Parliament remarks same day (ABC / Brisbane Times / Guardian). techAU 17 Sep on Zerra DA (lodged 17 Aug) and 1.44 GW IT / 2.16 GW peak figures from planning docs., via Reuters; Queensland Premier (Parliament); ABC News] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Bell × Saskatchewan MOU: up to +900 MW AI Fabric (path to 1.2 GW hub)
item.description: On 14 September 2026 Bell Canada and the Government of Saskatchewan announced a non-binding memorandum of understanding to expand Bell AI Fabric with phased development of up to 900 MW of additional capacity — creating a path to a 1.2 GW Canadian AI infrastructure hub in the province (Saskatchewan release: retain original 300 MW from the provincial grid plus up to 900 MW under Bring Your Own Power / partner natural-gas generation). Bell PR: closed-loop cooling (no municipal water); HQ of Bell AI Fabric national ecosystem in Saskatchewan; full-buildout capital including DC, tenant compute and related generation could exceed $50 billion; subject to customer commitments, commercial agreements, permits and environmental assessments. Country conversion: Canada gets a named provincial GW-path print with BYOP power — still MOU-gated, not a FID. [Signal 86, Primary Bell CNW 14 Sep 16:30 ET + Saskatchewan government release same day (1.2 GW path = 300 MW grid + ≤900 MW BYOP). Data Center News Canada; ConstructConnect/Canadian Press 15 Sep on Carney/Moe summit framing., via Bell Canada / CNW; Government of Saskatchewan] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: ERCOT issues State & Community Impact RFI for Batch Zero / medium data centers (due Oct 12)
item.description: On 14 September 2026 ERCOT Market Notice M-B091426-01 issued a State and Community Impact Request for Information to (1) ILLEs with Batch Zero conditional base/studied data-center loads not yet energized at ≥60 kV and (2) substantiated 25–<75 MW data-center developers from the Aug 19 Medium Load RFI. Complete notarized responses due 5pm CPT 12 October 2026 via RIOO; failure reported to PUC and the Governor. Same notice: Governor letter same day directs TWDB to partner with ERCOT/PUC on water source/consumption audit (Section C authorized by TWDB EA; non-response may carry Water Code penalties). Community Impact Review Report targeted with Eligibility Verification by 10 December 2026. Country conversion: Texas converts Abbott’s community/water directive into a binding RFI clock on the entire conditional Batch Zero book — separate from the Sep 9 eligibility RFI. [Signal 88, Primary ERCOT market notice 14 Sep 2026 5:07pm. Context: M-A080326-01 pause; Sep 9 eligibility RFI (M-A090926-01); Dec 10 filing target in ERCOT Batch Zero Update PDF (11 Sep)., via ERCOT Market Notice M-B091426-01] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: ERCOT discloses Batch Zero conditional split: 66.4 GW base / ~128 GW studied; 461-site community survey under Abbott audit
item.description: On 11 September 2026 ERCOT presented Batch Zero conditional classifications with public megawatt totals for the first time: 204 Large Load projects (66.4 GW) conditionally included as base load and 158 projects (~125.4–127.9 GW in board slides) as studied load, while 373 projects (~302.2 GW) were excluded. Interconnecting TSPs received provisional classifications on 3 Sep; final inclusion/exclusion follows eligibility verification and a community-impact review, both due to PUCT by 10 December 2026. ERCOT will survey 461 data centers (247 ≥75 MW large + 214 medium 25–75 MW) on water, cooling, ownership, financial assistance and community impact; verification RFIs continue with a late-September response clock. Energization of new ≥75 MW data centers and crypto remains paused. Country conversion: Texas AI/load path now has a quantified Base vs Studied vs Excluded book under audit — still conditional, still gated. [Signal 92, Primary ERCOT PDF for Board 14–15 Sep. Houston Public Media 11 Sep (Seely at PUCT: included MW totals and 461-site survey). Distinct from M-A080326-04 (3 Sep) which published classifications without public MW., via ERCOT Board Item 14 Batch Zero Update] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Chinese AI chipmakers raise Ascend/Cambricon indicated prices as HBM shortage bites
item.description: On 10 September 2026, Reuters reported (exclusive, three people familiar) that Huawei lifted the indicated price of its Ascend 950DT accelerator card to above 250,000 yuan (~$37,255) — 20–50% above quotes from two months earlier — with Q4 2026 availability previously stated by Huawei. Cambricon’s planned 690 chip was indicated 20–30% higher; MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX made similar moves, sources said. Ascend 950PR rose to >80,000 yuan from ~60,000 earlier in 2026; Ascend 910C to >110,000 from ~90,000. Drivers cited: advanced-HBM export curbs since Dec 2024 and grey-market HBM costs feeding into finished cards. Companies did not comment. Country conversion: domestic China AI accelerator economics reprice under HBM scarcity — a Pricing/Stall print on national compute substitution. [Signal 74, Reuters exclusive 10 Sep (anonymous sources). No company confirmation. Context: US advanced-HBM export controls since Dec 2024., via Reuters] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: NVIDIA names eight Australian partners for up to 2 GW DSX AI-factory buildout by 2027
item.description: On 9 September 2026, NVIDIA announced collaboration with Australian NVIDIA Cloud Partners and infrastructure operators Firmus, Sharon AI, IREN, Megaport, ResetData, CDC, NEXTDC and AirTrunk to expand land, power and powered-shell capacity for NVIDIA DSX AI factories — targeting up to a 2-gigawatt buildout by 2027. Partners operate the factories; NVIDIA supplies DSX platform, accelerated computing, networking and software. Named campus color includes IREN’s 800 MW Bundey (South Australia) and CDC’s >550 MW operating ANZ footprint with a further 800 MW under construction. No programme-wide capex figure or per-site energization schedule in the release. Country conversion: Australia gets an explicit national-scale AI-factory MW target tied to named operators, still gated by power delivery. [Signal 88, Primary NVIDIA Newsroom (9 Sep). Reuters Sydney 10 Sep; GlobeNewswire syndicate; techAU / TNW secondary., via NVIDIA Newsroom] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: IREN Sweetwater 2 GW hub conditionally classified Base Load in ERCOT Batch Zero
item.description: On 8 September 2026, IREN Limited (NASDAQ: IREN) announced that its 2 GW Sweetwater Hub — Sweetwater 1 (1,400 MW) and Sweetwater 2 (600 MW) in West Texas — was conditionally included as Base Load in ERCOT’s Batch Zero large-load interconnection process. Sweetwater 1’s high-voltage substation was energized earlier in 2026; construction of 300 MW (gross) of data-center capacity continues with delivery targeted for Q4 2027. Additional unnamed IREN pipeline projects also entered Batch Zero and will be disclosed only after grid-connection agreements. Classifications remain conditional and subject to ongoing ERCOT/PUCT verification. Country conversion: a named 2 GW Texas AI campus moves from opaque queue into the verified Base Load path under Batch Zero, still gated by post-classification audit. [Signal 90, Primary company PR (GlobeNewswire 8 Sep). Context: ERCOT M-A080326-04 Batch Zero conditional classifications (3 Sep); Construction Review Online 9 Sep; Markets Insider reprint of same PR., via IREN Limited / GlobeNewswire] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Firmus locks OpenAI as Malaysia AI Factory anchor — portfolio contracted capacity tops 900 MW
item.description: On 8 September 2026 Firmus announced a multi-year partnership under which OpenAI will contract dedicated AI compute from two Firmus AI Factory sites in Malaysia, making OpenAI an anchor customer. Firmus says total contracted capacity across customers now exceeds 900 MW. Its portfolio spans seven AI factories across Australia, Singapore, Indonesia and Malaysia (two operational today; five under development targeting ready-for-service within ~24 months). The Malaysia sites will use NVIDIA DSX with Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale systems integrated into Firmus HyperCube (prefab liquid-cooling/electrification from regional NSW). Firmus did not disclose Malaysia-site MW or contract value; Reuters separately noted Malaysia’s rapid DC buildout and electricity/water scrutiny. Country conversion: OpenAI-branded capacity path into Malaysia. [Signal 84, Reuters 8 Sep 2026 (Firmus–OpenAI Malaysia deal; contracted capacity >900 MW; Vera Rubin; portfolio AUS/SGP + five under development). Business Times Singapore same-day. NVIDIA quote on Firmus PR (DSX / Vera Rubin NVL72)., via Firmus] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Stargate Korea stalls: Samsung SDS and SKT say sites, power, and funding still unset a year after MOU
item.description: On 7 September 2026 Korea JoongAng Daily reported that nearly a year after OpenAI’s October 2025 Stargate Korea framing with Samsung and SK, neither data-center leg has settled site, power, water, or funding. Samsung SDS said “nothing has been confirmed” and the decision sits with OpenAI; SK Telecom said no progress since the MOU and OpenAI demand is not finalized; an OpenAI spokesperson said the domestic project is “still under discussion.” Industry sources cited power and water as the binding site constraints. The piece places Korea alongside paused Stargate legs in Norway and Britain. Separate from Korea’s AIDC 18.4 GW / budget track already on Wire — this is a conversion Stall on the OpenAI-branded campus path. [Signal 78, Multi-party, via Korea JoongAng Daily] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: TCS HyperVault locks 264 acres in Hyderabad for up to 1 GW AI campus — ₹70,000 crore with Telangana
item.description: On 5 September 2026 TCS subsidiary HyperVault announced it has secured 264 acres in Hyderabad (Telangana) to develop a phased AI data-center campus of up to 1 GW, purpose-built for frontier AI and hyperscaler GPU training/inference with liquid cooling and high rack density. Revanth Reddy publicly framed a June 2, 2028 inauguration target. TPG remains the named strategic capital partner from the earlier HyperVault raise. Conversion signal: India land + GW ceiling + state partnership are live; power offtake (PPA), EPC, and hyperscaler contracts were not disclosed in the press release. [Signal 88, Confirmed, via TCS / HyperVault press release] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: ERCOT issues Batch Zero conditional classifications to TSPs/DSPs — late vs Aug 31 clock
item.description: On 3 September 2026 at 15:55 CT, ERCOT Market Notice M-A080326-04 notified interconnecting TSPs/DSPs of provisional Batch Zero classifications for submitted Large Loads. Classifications may be conditional on ILLE verification, curing dynamic-model deficiencies, or a PUCT good-cause exception; failure to satisfy a condition may disqualify the load. ERCOT will not seek a GCE for every requested load. Reclassification disputes (base→studied) run under Planning Guide §9.3.1(2)(a) with a two-business-day TSP/DSP notify clock. No public MW list or names were published. Follows M-A080326-03 (31 Aug) delay past the PUCT-authorized 31 Aug conditional-classify target. Country conversion: Texas large-load study path unfreezes into a conditional, dispute-gated Batch Zero. [Signal 88, Primary ERCOT notice. Context: M-A080326-03 delay (31 Aug); PUCT Project 59142 GCE order (20 Aug); Texas Dispatch 4 Sep on Sep 11 Project 58481 permanent large-load rule vote., via ERCOT Market Notice M-A080326-04] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Fervo signs 396 MW, 15-year Google PPA at Cape Station — foundation for a potential Utah data center
item.description: On 1 September 2026 Fervo Energy (Nasdaq: FRVO) announced a 396 MW power purchase agreement with Google for enhanced-geothermal output from the Cape Station GeoCluster in Beaver County, Utah. Fervo's 8-K dates the contract to 26 August 2026 between wholly owned Cape Generating Station 6 LLC and Google Energy LLC: four successive 99 MW sub-tranches with target commercial operation beginning Q3 2028, a 15-year delivery term, and parent guarantees from Fervo and Alphabet. Fervo will offer Google an option to add roughly 600 MW — nearly 1 GW in total — with a guaranteed COD no later than June 2030, and may owe Google reimbursement of certain payments if it fails to make that expansion offer. Google describes the energy as a foundational building block for a potential Utah data center; final data-center plans stay subject to engineering, state and local approvals and commercial conditions, with delivery leaning on Utah SB 132 direct-to-load pathways. Billed as the largest enhanced-geothermal PPA to date. [Signal 90, Confirmed, via Fervo Energy IR / FRVO 8-K] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Korea's 2027 budget proposal nearly doubles AI and chip spend to ₩21.3T, with ₩3.85T for 10,000 Vera Rubin-class GPUs
item.description: The Korean cabinet approved a record ₩820.9 trillion 2027 budget proposal on 1 September 2026, up 12.8% and the fastest increase on record, funded by semiconductor-boom tax revenue. Spending on AI plus the administration's three megaprojects — semiconductors, physical AI and AI data centres — nearly doubles from ₩10.8T this year to ₩21.3T. The Ministry of Science and ICT's own budget rises 24.5% to ₩29.65T, with AI up 84.3% to ₩9.4T, including ₩3.85T (from ₩2.08T) to add about 10,000 Nvidia Vera Rubin-class GPUs for sovereign models behind a free 'AI for All' service, ₩87.8B for an AI-data-centre cluster and a 10 MW AIDC testbed; roughly ₩2T goes to a semiconductor special account and more than ₩2T to power, water and industrial complexes. The proposal goes to the National Assembly on 3 September and must pass by 2 December, so this is budgeted intent, not yet appropriated. [Signal 80, Confirmed, via Yonhap / Hankyoreh / Korea Herald / MSIT budget detail via Digital Today] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: EuroHPC signs €387.8M LUMI-AI contract with Bull — an MI430X AI factory in Kajaani, Finland
item.description: On 31 August 2026 the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking signed a procurement contract with Bull to deploy the LUMI-AI supercomputer at CSC – IT Center for Science's data centre in Kajaani, Finland. Total budget for acquisition, delivery, installation and maintenance is €387,800,000, funded 50% by EuroHPC from the Digital Europe Programme and 50% by the LUMI AI Factory consortium — Finland, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Norway and Poland. The system is built on next-generation AMD Instinct MI430X GPUs with 6th Gen 256-core AMD EPYC processors and is expected to deliver roughly ten times the AI capacity of the current LUMI, installed and available to users in 2027. Bull was selected from a tender launched in May 2025; Finland was picked as host in December 2024. This is EuroHPC's sixth AI Factory procurement contract, and a rare flagship European win for AMD accelerators. [Signal 84, Confirmed, via EuroHPC JU / Bull] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: HUMAIN's MI355X compute goes live in Saudi Arabia; JV plans up to 250 MW of MI400 capacity from 2027
item.description: AMD, Cisco and HUMAIN — a PIF company — announced on 31 August 2026 that AMD Instinct MI355X GPU infrastructure built on Cisco Silicon One networking with 800G optics is live in Saudi Arabia and serving customers in the Kingdom and beyond, offered as GPU-as-a-service from training to inference. It is the first production milestone of the joint venture the three announced on 19 November 2025. The next phase is up to 250 MW powered by AMD Instinct MI400-series GPUs, EPYC CPUs and ROCm with Cisco networking, deployment beginning in 2027 and capacity expected to start coming online in the second half of that year; the JV still says it is on track for up to 1 GW by 2030. No megawatt figure, customer count, utilization or pricing was disclosed for the live system, and the original phase-1 plan named 100 MW of MI450 — so the announced path has shifted. [Signal 72, Single-source, via AMD IR / Cisco Newsroom] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Anthropic reported to take ~350 MW at Hut 8's Beacon Point via a $35B Lambda contract, with Nvidia on the lease
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reported on 31 August 2026, matched by Bloomberg and Reuters citing people familiar, that Anthropic signed a roughly $35B, six-year cloud contract with Nvidia-backed Lambda for about 350 MW at Hut 8's Beacon Point campus in Nueces County, Texas — close to one of the site's ~352 MW phases. Reporting describes a four-party chain: Hut 8 develops and leases the space, Nvidia holds the master lease and supplies the GPUs, Lambda installs them and sells capacity to Anthropic. Hut 8 disclosed in July two 15-year leases totalling about 704 MW with $19.6B of base-term value to an unnamed investment-grade tenant later reported to be Nvidia; initial energization of the ~1 GW campus is expected in Q1 2027. None of Anthropic, Lambda, Nvidia or Hut 8 has confirmed the contract, and Lambda's payment to Nvidia is undisclosed, so treat the $35B as reported rather than filed. [Signal 70, Corroborated, via WSJ (first) / Bloomberg / Reuters via CNA / Hut 8 July disclosure] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: US Commerce drafts remote-access rule to curb China rental of advanced GPUs via third-country DCs
item.description: Late August 2026 reporting (Forbes 31 Aug; TechTimes 29 Aug citing The Information) says Trump Commerce/BIS is preparing an export-control draft that would treat remote rental of advanced AI GPUs as controlled access, aimed at Chinese firms using third-country data centers such as Thailand and Singapore, with industry draft circulation possible as early as September. The House already passed the Remote Access Security Act (H.R. 2683) in January; the Senate has not. Export-control bar commentary notes BIS’s statutory remote-access authority is weak until RASA clears. This is a Policy/Stall conversion signal on usable FLOPs geography, not a published final rule. [Signal 72, Corroborated, via Forbes / TechTimes / Congress.gov H.R.2683] More: https://compute.world/wire.html
